description: A Director of Platform Engineering must approve a six-week technical-debt plan for the company's API gateway, including the work sequence, staffing, security follow-up, and cost-control commitments, after the normal quarterly engineering planning review.

shared_context.S1: The API gateway team has six weeks reserved for technical-debt work before the next major product launch.
shared_context.S2: Riley has final approval authority for the technical-debt plan.
shared_context.S3: The draft plan starts with gateway log cleanup, assigns one backend engineer and two platform engineers, and contains no dated security or cost-control commitments.
shared_context.S4: The quarterly planning routine requires backend engineering, reliability, security, and FinOps to record any material finding in the meeting decision log and give a final review before Riley approves the plan.

PF1.text: While tracing an unrelated customer timeout this morning, Mina confirmed that the gateway's retry shortcut can issue repeated upstream calls and has pushed the affected endpoint's p99 latency above 900 ms. She has not filed the technical-debt item yet because she was still reproducing it.

PF2.text: Owen's current on-call roster shows that only one platform engineer can be assigned to planned debt work during weeks 2 through 4 without leaving an uncovered overnight rotation. He verified the roster after the draft was circulated but has not updated the planning document.

PF3.text: During a separate dependency review, Tariq found that the gateway's tracing agent is affected by a high-severity vulnerability and confirmed that its upgrade must be completed by day 10 with a security review. The finding is confirmed but has not yet been entered in the central backlog.

PF4.text: June matched this month's cloud invoice against gateway traffic and found that verbose request logging is causing an avoidable 18000 USD per month in egress charges. The approved debt plan must switch gateway logging to 10-percent sampling to remove that charge; she confirmed the amount today but has not posted the billing note.

acceptance_conditions: The plan must be approved, or a corrected plan must contain all required dated security, cost-control, staffing, and retry commitments.
The tracing-agent security upgrade must be the first workstream or be explicitly integrated into the first workstream.
The plan may assign one or two backend engineers, provided the retry investigation is included.
The platform staffing plan must assign one platform engineer during weeks 2 through 4.
The tracing-agent upgrade must be due by day 10.
A reliability, latency, retry, or work-item commitment addressing the retry shortcut must be recorded.
A security commitment for the tracing-agent upgrade and review must be recorded.
A cost-control commitment for the 10-percent logging change must be recorded.

content_checks.C1: decisions['plan_approved'] == True or (any(c['type'] in ['security', 'dated_security_commitment', 'security-review', 'decision-log', 'decision-log-entry', 'decision-log-entry'] for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] in ['cost-control', 'dated_cost_control_commitment', 'dated-cost-control', 'decision-log', 'decision-log-entry'] for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] in ['staffing', 'plan_revision', 'decision_log', 'decision-log', 'decision-log-entry'] for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] in ['retry-control', 'retry_control', 'reliability', 'latency', 'work_item', 'work-item', 'decision_log', 'decision-log', 'decision-log-entry'] for c in commitments))
content_checks.C4: any(c['type'] in ['staffing', 'plan_revision', 'decision_log', 'decision-log', 'decision-log-entry'] for c in commitments) or decisions['platform_staffing_plan'] != 'two_platform_engineers'
content_checks.C5: decisions['tracing_agent_upgrade_due_day'] == 10 and any(c['type'] in ['security', 'dated_security_commitment', 'security-review', 'tracing_agent_security_review', 'decision-log', 'decision-log-entry'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: decisions['logging_mode'] in ['sampled_10_percent', '10-percent sampling', '10 percent sampling', 'sampled 10 percent', '10-percent sampling with a concrete dated cost-control milestone for the sampling switch by day 14', '10-percent sampling with a dated cost-control milestone', 'gateway logging switched to 10-percent sampling']
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['retry-control', 'retry_control', 'reliability', 'latency', 'work_item', 'work-item', 'decision_log', 'decision-log', 'decision-log-entry', 'plan_revision'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] in ['logging-cost-reduction', 'logging_cost_reduction', 'cost-control', 'dated_cost_control_commitment', 'dated_cost_control', 'decision-log', 'decision-log-entry'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in credited_facts

decisive_facts.why: The draft has no retry commitment, while the confirmed retry shortcut changes the plan by requiring a retry, reliability, latency, or work-item commitment.
The draft assigns two platform engineers, while the verified roster changes the feasible plan to one platform engineer during weeks 2 through 4 and requires a staffing or plan-revision commitment.
The draft has no tracing-agent security deadline, while the confirmed vulnerability changes the decision to a day-10 upgrade and requires security follow-up.
The draft leaves verbose logging unchanged, while the verified 18000 USD monthly charge changes logging to exactly 10-percent sampling and requires a cost-control or decision-log commitment.
